verses.text: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for fifty-five years. His mother was Hephzibah.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes. He copied the disgusting practices of the nations the LORD had driven out ahead of the Israelites.

He rebuilt the high places his father Hezekiah had destroyed. He set up altars to Baal and made an Asherah pole, as Ahab king of Israel had done. He bowed down to all the stars in the sky and worshipped them.
He built altars in the LORD's temple, the place where the LORD had said, "I will put my name in Jerusalem."
In both courtyards of the LORD's temple, he built altars to all the stars in the sky.

He sacrificed his own son in the fire. He practised magic and fortune-telling, and he went to people who talk with spirits of the dead and to people who claim to know the future. He did a great deal of evil in the LORD's eyes and made him angry.

He took the carved Asherah idol he had made and put it in the temple. This was the temple about which the LORD had said to David and his son Solomon, "In this temple and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever.

I will never again make the Israelites wander from the land I gave their ancestors, if only they will be careful to do everything I have commanded them, and obey all the Law my servant Moses gave them."
But the people did not listen. Manasseh led them into doing even more evil than the nations the LORD had destroyed ahead of the Israelites.
So the LORD spoke through his servants the prophets. He said,
"Manasseh king of Judah has done these disgusting things. He has done more evil than the Amorites who lived here before him, and he has led Judah into sin with his idols.
So this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I am going to bring such disaster on Jerusalem and Judah that the ears of everyone who hears about it will ring.

I will measure Jerusalem with the same measuring line I used against Samaria, and the same plumb line I used against Ahab's family. I will wipe Jerusalem clean as someone wipes a dish, wiping it and turning it upside down.
I will abandon the rest of my people who are left, and I will hand them over to their enemies. All their enemies will rob them and carry off their things,
because they have done what is evil in my eyes. They have made me angry from the day their ancestors came out of Egypt until today.'"

Manasseh also killed so many innocent people that he filled Jerusalem with their blood from one end to the other. This was in addition to the sin he led Judah into, doing what was evil in the LORD's eyes.
The rest of what Manasseh did, all his deeds and the sin he committed, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
Manasseh died and was buried in the garden of his own palace, the garden of Uzza. His son Amon became king after him.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for two years. His mother was Meshullemeth, the daughter of Haruz, from Jotbah.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, as his father Manasseh had done.
He followed all the ways of his father. He worshipped the idols his father had worshipped, and bowed down to them.
He turned away from the LORD, the God of his ancestors, and did not walk in the LORD's ways.
Amon's officials made a plot against him and killed the king in his palace.
But the people of the land killed all those who had plotted against King Amon. Then they made his son Josiah king in his place.
The rest of what Amon did is written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
He was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza. His son Josiah became king after him.
